content:
Alex: quick check — I'm proposing a small change to the convo streaming shape for tool/function calls. Current problem: we sometimes re-emit the entire function_call payload on every delta chunk which inflates bandwidth and complicates reassembly. Proposal: emit a compact lifecycle stream: a single `tool_call.start` event, then `delta` chunks with only the content fragments, then `tool_call.end` with the final result metadata. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4387 :eyes:

Mai: can you paste a tiny example of the proposed stream frames? want to see exact fields (clients parse pretty strictly).

Alex: sure — minimal example:
```json
{ "type": "tool_call.start", "name": "search", "args": { "q": "k8s scheduling" } }
{ "type": "delta", "content": "Found 3 results: \n- pod evictions\n- taint issues\n" }
{ "type": "delta", "content": "More details..." }
{ "type": "tool_call.end", "result": "{\"items\":[...]}" }
```

CJ: quick note from SDK side — our JS SDK historically accepted either full `function_call` objects per chunk or incremental `delta` with a `function_call` only at the start. We can adapt to `tool_call.*` naming but need a compatibility layer. Are we renaming `function_call` -> `tool_call` across the board?

Alex: yes, plan is to standardize on `tool_call` in the new contract (more explicit for external tool runner). But we must keep compatibility: the server will continue emitting `function_call` aliases for clients that request legacy mode for at least one minor release.

Taylor: +1. For rollout, can we gate this behind a model-route flag? e.g. `streaming_toolcall_mode: \"compact\" | \"full\"` so we can flip on per-customer and canary without breaking everyone.

Alex: exactly what I had in mind. Default stays `full` for now; we'll enable `compact` by route as we validate behavior.

Mai: what about streaming parsers that expect `content` field only on `delta` frames? Will they choke if we include small metadata on each delta (e.g., seq ids)?

Alex: we plan to keep deltas tiny — only `content` and optional `seq`. The only metadata that might appear is `seq` and `eof: true` on the final delta if `tool_call.end` is not used. But recommended pattern is `tool_call.end` for finalization.

CJ: I'll add a compatibility shim in the JS SDK parser: accept `tool_call.start` + `delta` + `tool_call.end` flow, and continue supporting older `function_call` chunking. I'll also emit an SDK warning when `tool_call.*` is detected on older runtime versions.

SREBot: FYI — if we start emitting fewer bytes per stream, network e2e might look different; please add a perf check for connection churn vs steady state throughput.

Taylor: I'll add unit + e2e tests: parser tests (ordering, missing start, missing end), and network tests with partial chunks. Also add a test ensuring older clients (simulated) still parse via alias.

Alex: awesome. CI on the PR currently: DeployBot reports streaming-tests on linux passed, but a flaky test in parser-suite on mac. Link: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/9876 :white_check_mark::question:

DeployBot: streaming-tests: 142 passed, 1 flaky (parser-suite.test.ts) — rerun scheduled.

Mai: parity question — do we still include `content_type` (e.g., \"text/markdown\") on `delta` frames? some downstream renderers need it.

Alex: we'll include `content_type` only on `tool_call.start` and `tool_call.end` as metadata. Deltas are purely content fragments. That keeps the streaming parser simpler.

CJ: noted. I'll update SDK docs and add a migration snippet for teams that reassemble function payloads. Want me to draft the CHANGELOG entry?

Alex: please do. Also add an example in streaming.md showing how to reassemble to legacy shape.

Taylor: pinging @CJ for code review once I push tests. I will also create a small canary config that flips `streaming_toolcall_mode=compact` for 1% of traffic on dedicated infra.

Mai: lgtm pending tests and CI green. Also add a short note in the deprecation guide about timeline and rollback strategy.

Alex: thank you — plan: merge behind feature flag after CI, enable canary tomorrow morning, monitor error-rate and SDK parse errors. I'll post a short follow-up in #deploy if anything unusual shows up.

CJ: I'll watch the telemetry and be ready to ship an SDK patch if we see parse errors.

Taylor: created test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4392 — includes parser tests + canary config.

Alex: sweet. Closing the loop: thanks everyone, will update thread when canary starts. :sparkles:
